test_title: SSC Stenographer 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 13 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.

Ravina was very sick today, and __we will take her to the hospital as she gets worse.__

options.text: we will take her to the hospital now before she gets worse
we can take her to the hospital now before she get worse
we took her to the hospital now before she gets worse

solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the future tense, indicating a plan or intention to take Ravina to the hospital.
 
• The underlined segment **"as she gets worse"** suggests a condition that triggers the action of taking Ravina to the hospital.
 
• The phrase **"now before she gets worse"** conveys a sense of urgency, aligning with the context of Ravina being very sick.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **'we will take her to the hospital now before she gets worse.'**

Therefore, the correct answer is -** 'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Option 2:** This option contains a subject-verb agreement error. "She" requires the singular verb form "gets," not "get."
 
• **Option 3:** No substitution is needed as the original underlined segment is grammatically correct and contextually appropriate.
 
• **Option 4:** This option changes the tense of the sentence to past tense, which doesn't match the original future tense context. Additionally, the placement of "now" is awkward in this context.
